record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Examine locally spherical chiral 5-polytopes of hyperbolic type.

evidence.quote: Problem 14 Examine locally spherical chiral 5-polytopes of hyperbolic type.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract 5-polytope is a partially ordered set whose elements (called faces) have ranks in {-1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}, with a unique minimum face (rank -1) and unique maximum face (rank 5), such that every maximal chain (flag) has length 7, the poset is strongly flag-connected, and for any two faces F < G with rank(G) - rank(F) = 2, there are exactly two faces H with F < H < G (the diamond condition). 

A 5-polytope P is called chiral if its automorphism group has exactly two orbits on flags such that adjacent flags lie in different orbits (equivalently, P admits all "rotational" symmetries but no reflective symmetries). P is called locally spherical if all of its proper sections of rank ≤ 4 (its facets and vertex-figures, together with their iterated facets/vertex-figures) are isomorphic to convex spherical polytopes, i.e. each facet and each vertex-figure has a Schläfli-type symbol whose associated Coxeter group is finite (spherical). P is said to be of hyperbolic type if its Schläfli symbol {p_1, p_2, p_3, p_4} is one of the symbols whose associated rank-5 Coxeter group is a compact hyperbolic Coxeter group, namely {3,3,3,5}, {5,3,3,3}, {3,3,5,3}, {3,5,3,3}, {3,4,3,3,...} of compact hyperbolic type in rank 5 (more precisely, the Schläfli symbols {3,3,3,5}, {5,3,3,3}, {3,3,5,3}, {5,3,3,5}, {5,3,3,4}, {4,3,3,5}).

Problem: Investigate locally spherical chiral 5-polytopes of hyperbolic type. In particular, determine whether finite such polytopes exist; if so, construct examples (especially with small or with infinitely many automorphism groups), and classify them up to isomorphism.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to be still largely open. While recent work has produced finite examples of locally spherical regular (reflexible) hypertopes of hyperbolic type in rank 5, and constructions of chiral polytopes of small rank have been developed using GPR-graphs, the literature does not yet provide a classification or systematic theory of locally spherical chiral 5-polytopes of hyperbolic type.

status_evidence.title: Proper locally spherical hypertopes of hyperbolic type
status_evidence.snippet: CPR-graphs used to build infinite families of locally spherical regular hypertopes for each Coxeter diagram of hyperbolic type of ranks 4 and 5; first finite rank-5 example produced.
status_evidence.claim: Existence results for the regular (non-chiral) analogue have only recently been obtained, indicating the chiral case remains under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Constructions of Chiral Polytopes of Small Rank
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of chiral polytopes of small rank using generalized permutation representation graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Constructions of chiral polytopes of rank 5 exist but a study of the locally spherical hyperbolic case is not completed.
